column1: # boru Language Specification: Dispatch edge cases 1 — overload order,
# first-match over sorted signatures, the add numeric-vs-concat lattice,
# Dispatch is type-directed: a word's signatures are sorted at
# first, then per position the more specific type first, stable for
# ties — and matchSignature then takes the FIRST match over that
# sorted order. So listing order in a `def … fn` is irrelevant except
# as a tie-break; a leaf type always beats its ancestor at the same
# `add` is the canonical overload lattice (see EXPLANATION.md
# [Scalar String] concatenate — so concatenation fires only when AT
# LEAST ONE operand is a String; every other Scalar pairing (Boolean +
# Integer, Atom + Integer, …) matches no overload and raises
# §1  add concat lattice — positives (result = args[1] ++ args[0])

column3: [Scalar String]: the Integer coerces, String-first concat order
[String Scalar]: mirror slot order concatenates the other way round
mixed split: a→sig0, 1→sig1 → '1'++'a'
mixed split the other way: 1→sig0, a→sig1 → 'a'++'1'
mixed split with two strings: b→sig0, a→sig1 → 'a'++'b'
stack form: top b→sig0, deeper a→sig1 — mirror-equivalent to the mixed split
Boolean + String: the String slot admits concat, Boolean coerces
String + Boolean: same lattice, mirrored slots
Atom + String: an Atom is a Scalar, so it coerces into concat
mixed split: cat→sig0(Scalar), x→sig1(String) → 'x'++'cat'
EmptyString is still a String — concat with the empty string
String + Boolean via the empty string: coercion, not truthiness
Float + String: the Float's string form is spliced in

column1: # §2  add concat lattice — negatives ([boru/signature_error]: no overload)

column3: Boolean + Integer: neither operand is a String
mixed split of the same pair fails identically
and the other mixed split too — no slot order admits it

column2: ERROR:arithmetic is not defined on Boolean
column3: two Booleans: the within-type defined error (Boolean carries the logical words)
Atom + Integer: Atom is a Scalar but not a String
mixed split of Atom + Integer fails identically
two Atoms concatenate names within-type (b-op-a: forward form computes dog add cat)
Atom + Boolean: same story
Boolean + Float: a Number operand does not rescue a Boolean
none is not a Number
…and not a Scalar either: even a String cannot concat none
none + none matches nothing
Map + Integer: compounds are outside the add lattice
Map + String: a String does not admit a compound partner
List + List: no concat through add — lists have their own words
a bare type literal is not a concrete Number
the String TYPE literal is not a concrete String — no concat
type literal in the Scalar slot fails the same way
Float partner promotes the result to Float
…pinned via typeof
promotion is slot-symmetric
Integer + Integer stays Integer
mixed split promotes identically

column1: # §4  numeric promotion — the Big leaves (exact types never mix with Float)

column3: Integer + BigInteger → BigInteger
slot-symmetric
…pinned via typeof
Integer + BigDecimal → BigDecimal
…pinned via typeof
BigInteger + BigDecimal → BigDecimal (widest exact leaf)
Float + BigInteger is a type_error, not a silent binary-float demotion
slot-symmetric compile failure
Float + BigDecimal declines identically
pure forward form declines too
but a String partner still concats a BigInteger — its 0d literal form is spliced in

column1: # §5  concat is add-only — the other math words have no String overload

column3: sub has only numeric signatures
no Python-style string repetition through mul
two Strings divide within-type: occurrence count of "a" in "b" (forward form computes b div a)
mod rejects Boolean like add does
pow rejects a String base

column1: # §6  user-fn overloads — most-specific-first, NOT listing order

column3: leaf listed first, leaf wins
ancestor listed first — the leaf STILL wins (sigs are specificity-sorted)
a Float misses the Integer sig and lands on Number
Any is the last resort even when listed first
deeper lattice node beats the shallower one
a Boolean misses Number and falls to Any
Any catches what the leaf rejects
exact tie: stable sort keeps listing order — first listed wins
a List matches neither overload — no silent Any degrade

column1: def g fn [[x:Integer y:Any][String]["IA"] [x:Any y:Integer][String]["AI"]] g 1 2
column3: per-position specificity is lexicographic: position 0 outranks position 1

column1: def g fn [[x:Any y:Integer][String]["AI"] [x:Integer y:Any][String]["IA"]] g 1 2
column3: …and reversing the listing does not change that
longer arity sorts first: the 2-arg sig takes both args
a Node-branch leaf beats Any as well
…and an Integer falls through Map to Any
listing order irrelevant on the Node branch too

column1: # §6b  disjunct-typed params — `tor` unions in the overload order
def g fn [[x:(Integer tor String)][String]["ok"]] g 1
column3: a disjunct param admits its first alternative

column1: def g fn [[x:(Integer tor String)][String]["ok"]] g "a"
column3: …and its second

column1: def g fn [[x:(Integer tor String)][String]["ok"]] g true
column3: …and rejects everything outside the union

column1: def g fn [[x:(Integer tor String)][String]["dis"] [x:Integer][String]["int"]] g 1
column3: a disjunct sig outranks a bare leaf sig for a value both admit

column1: def g fn [[x:Integer][String]["int"] [x:(Integer tor String)][String]["dis"]] g 1
column3: …independent of listing order — the sort decides
